title: Final Exam: Shopify Plus Commerce Engineering
description: Thirty questions across the whole course — Liquid and theme architecture, storefront craft, performance and APIs, the Plus platform, B2B wholesale, POS and platform ownership. Aim for 80%. Sixty minutes.

questions.prompt: Why do Liquid typos rarely produce visible errors, and what follows from that?
options: They are caught at build time, so nothing follows
Undefined objects render as empty strings and missing snippets render nothing, with the page still returning 200 — so linting and review are the theme's error handling
Shopify emails the developer on a render error
They throw in the theme editor but not on the storefront
questions.explanation: There is no runtime exception to catch. Theme Check in the editor, in CI, and a review checklist are the only mechanisms that surface these before a customer does.

questions.prompt: Which are true of `{% render %}`? Select all that apply.
options: The snippet sees only globals plus explicitly passed arguments
Variables assigned inside cannot leak back to the caller
Its output can be cached because its inputs are explicit
It supports recursion for nested navigation
questions.explanation: Scope isolation is the point, and it is what makes output cacheable. Recursion is not possible, which is why every Shopify theme hand-unrolls nested menus to a fixed depth.

questions.prompt: A section renders as an empty box when a merchandiser adds it from the Add section menu. Most likely cause?
options: The preset supplies no defaults and the markup has no placeholder or empty-state fallback
questions.explanation: A freshly added section renders with only its preset's settings. Defaults, starter blocks in the preset and `placeholder_svg_tag` fallbacks are the quality bar — a section that looks broken on first add gets removed and reported as not working.

questions.prompt: A certification has a code, a badge image and a description, and is shared across dozens of products. Correct model?
options: A tag per certification parsed in Liquid
A list metafield plus a Liquid case statement mapping codes to badges
A metaobject referenced from products by a list.metaobject_reference metafield
questions.explanation: It has its own fields and is reused, so it is an entity. A case statement duplicates content into code where merchandisers cannot maintain it; tags carry no structure at all.

questions.prompt: Why is lazy-loading the LCP image one of the most reliable ways to fail that metric?
options: Lazy images are served at lower quality
It delays the browser's discovery and fetch of the element that defines the metric
questions.explanation: LCP has four phases, and load delay is one of them. `loading="lazy"` on the hero pushes discovery past the point where the browser would otherwise have started fetching. Eager loading plus a preload with fetchpriority is the fix.

questions.prompt: A cart holds the same variant twice with different line item properties. A per-line quantity control changes one. Which endpoint?
options: change.js keyed by the line item key
questions.explanation: update.js is keyed by variant ID and cannot distinguish the two lines. change.js targets a line by its key — the variant ID plus a hash of its properties.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine advantages of the Section Rendering API for cart and variant updates? Select all that apply.
options: Pricing and discount logic exists once, in Liquid
Merchant theme-editor settings apply with no code change
Function-based and B2B catalog pricing are computed correctly server-side
It removes the network round trip
questions.explanation: It does not remove the round trip — that is its cost. What it removes is the second implementation of pricing logic in JavaScript, which is where drift and B2B pricing errors come from.

questions.prompt: A Lighthouse score of 91 coexists with field data showing LCP at 3.8s. What is the primary reason?
options: Lab data is one synthetic run on a fixed profile; field data is the 75th percentile of real devices, networks and cache states
Field data lags by 28 days and is therefore stale
The two measure different pages by definition
questions.explanation: They measure different things. Field data is what Google ranks on and what a customer on a mid-range Android on a building site actually experiences.

questions.prompt: Marketing wants a new analytics vendor's snippet in theme.liquid. Correct response?
options: Add it to the head to capture everything
Implement it as a custom web pixel — sandboxed, off the main thread, consent-aware, and able to see checkout events
Add it deferred at the end of body
Decline; third-party analytics always harms performance
questions.explanation: Routing the request to the correct mechanism is the job. Declining outright is not, and pasting it into the theme puts a vendor script on your main thread with access to your DOM.

questions.prompt: An Admin GraphQL mutation returns HTTP 200 with a populated `userErrors` array. What happened?
options: It did not apply — userErrors carries business validation failures that do not produce an HTTP error
questions.explanation: This is GraphQL's equivalent of Liquid's silent failure. An integration that checks only HTTP status will fail to write data and nobody will notice for weeks.

questions.prompt: How is Shopify's GraphQL Admin API rate limiting modelled?
options: A leaky bucket of calculated query cost with a maximum capacity and a per-second restore rate
questions.explanation: Cost is calculated per field. Every response reports requestedQueryCost, actualQueryCost and throttleStatus, which lets a good client slow down before being throttled. Plus gets a larger bucket, not an unlimited one.

questions.prompt: After a release, merchandisers report yesterday's promotional section has vanished from product pages. Cause?
options: An invalid schema removed conflicting sections
The release shipped a `templates/product.json` based on an older state, overwriting theme editor edits
The GitHub integration reverted the file
questions.explanation: JSON templates are code and merchant data simultaneously. When a template change is genuinely part of a release: announce a freeze, pull current live JSON, merge onto it, deploy that file explicitly, then tell the team.

questions.prompt: What changes when the live theme is connected to `main` via the GitHub integration?
options: Theme editor changes commit back to main, so you must pull before branching and cannot treat main as code-only
All deploys must use the CLI
questions.explanation: The two-way sync is desirable — merchandising work becomes versioned and cannot be silently clobbered — but your protected branch now receives commits from people who have never used Git.

questions.prompt: Order the stages of rendering a Shopify product page.
items: Sections render their blocks and settings
The URL resolves to a template file
The template lists which sections appear, in what order
answer: The URL resolves to a template file
The template lists which sections appear, in what order
Sections render their blocks and settings
questions.explanation: Holding this chain in your head makes almost every 'where does this markup come from' question answerable in seconds — including when a template suffix is routing to an alternate template.

questions.prompt: Why can a Shopify Function not query your ERP at run time?
options: Functions run sandboxed as WebAssembly with no network access, a strict instruction budget, and a determinism requirement
The Admin API does not expose ERP data
questions.explanation: The sandbox is what makes Functions safe inside the checkout path. External data must already be on the store, typically synced into a metafield and read through the input query.

questions.prompt: A discount Function receives a malformed configuration metafield. Correct behaviour?
options: Throw so the error is visible
questions.explanation: A missing discount is a support ticket; an unintended discount is real money applied to every affected order until someone notices. Write the failure path first and make it the safe one.

questions.prompt: Match each requirement to the correct platform mechanism.

pairs.left: Different prices for a wholesale tier
Hide express shipping for hazardous goods
Capture a delivery date at checkout
pairs.right: Checkout UI extension writing a cart attribute

pairs.left: Notify a sales rep when a large order arrives

questions.explanation: Prices are catalogs, rules are Functions, checkout content and fields are UI extensions, reactions are Flow. Most defects in a multi-channel implementation come from mixing these up.

questions.prompt: In Shopify's native B2B model, at what level is pricing resolved?
questions.explanation: Catalogs are assigned to company locations, so one company's branches can be on different tiers. This is why a tag-based wholesale implementation cannot be retrofitted onto a real distribution business.

questions.prompt: Native B2B can be enabled on a store still using the classic customer account system.
questions.explanation: B2B requires the newer customer accounts; classic has nowhere for company context to live. On an inherited store this migration is a prerequisite, and it changes login flows and all account page work.

questions.prompt: A £500 trade minimum is enforced by JavaScript in the cart. A rep creates a £300 draft order. What happens?
options: It is rejected — minimums apply account-wide
It proceeds; theme validation does not apply to draft orders, the API or POS
Shopify enforces it once a company is attached
The buyer is blocked at the invoice page
questions.explanation: Anything commercially meaningful belongs in a cart and checkout validation Function. Being able to state which of your rules are platform-enforced and which are theme-enforced is a real architectural artefact.

questions.prompt: Which Flow trigger silently stops firing once payment terms are introduced?
questions.explanation: A terms order is created unpaid, so payment-keyed automations never fire — with no error, just orders quietly not reaching the warehouse. Auditing every automation and report keyed on payment is the most important B2B launch task.

questions.prompt: A quick order grid collects quantities for 40 variants. How should it add them?
options: One /cart/add.js request with an items array
questions.explanation: One round trip, no rate limiting, and no partial cart to reconcile after a mid-sequence failure. Per-line validation errors come back identified so you can show them against the offending row.

questions.prompt: Where should a per-account free-carriage threshold live?
options: In a company metafield read by the Function's input query
questions.explanation: The recurring principle of the whole course: put variation in data, not code. Sales ops changes a metafield; one Function serves every account; nobody deploys.

questions.prompt: A POS UI extension needs privileged store data. What is the correct trust boundary?
options: An Admin API token embedded in the extension
A session token from the extension, verified by your backend, which makes the Admin API call
questions.explanation: The extension runs on a device in a shop and must never hold an Admin token. This is the same boundary as an app proxy on the storefront.

questions.prompt: A business will open eight stores in two years. Which decision at store one most reduces the cost of store eight?
options: Location-specific data in metafields or metaobjects, and no hard-coded location IDs anywhere
A separate Shopify store per location
questions.explanation: If store details are data and nothing references a location by ID, opening a store is a JSON file, a script run and a runbook. Otherwise every opening is a development project.

questions.prompt: Which rules make a webhook consumer reliable? Select all that apply.
options: Be idempotent, because delivery is at-least-once
Reconcile on a schedule, because events can be missed
questions.explanation: All four. Unverified endpoints accept forged payloads, slow endpoints get retried then unsubscribed, duplicates are normal, and reconciliation is how you find the gaps before finance does.

questions.prompt: Which app evaluation question is most often skipped and most often expensive on a three-channel store?
options: Does it support B2B and POS, or only DTC?
questions.explanation: Most apps are DTC-only. On a store sharing one catalogue across three channels, a pricing or badging app that ignores catalog pricing shows a wrong price to a trade buyer.

questions.prompt: What makes an engineering standard real rather than aspirational?
options: Tooling that fails a build, plus explicit checklist items in the PR template — applied identically to internal and external contributors
questions.explanation: Enforcement is the whole difference. It also depersonalises cross-organisation review: a failed check is a fact, whereas a preference is an opinion that produces a meeting.

questions.prompt: As the only internal Shopify developer, which practice most reduces business risk?
options: Documentation and runbooks that let someone else operate the platform in your absence
questions.explanation: A bus factor of one is the largest risk on a solo-owned platform, and inventories, runbooks and decision records are the only lever on it. Tests protect the code; documentation protects the business's ability to run without you.

questions.prompt: Name the two file paths that hold merchant-owned theme editor data and must never be blindly overwritten on deploy. Either one is accepted.
questions.explanation: `config/settings_data.json` holds theme settings values; `templates/*.json` hold the section manifests merchandisers arrange. Both are simultaneously code and production data, which is the single most distinctive operational hazard in Shopify theme development.
